user_visible_outcome: A declared 'verified_free' coverage claim can no longer be published on evidence that has expired, and a declared 'verified_free' claim the published catalogue has never corroborated can no longer sit in the catalogue forever without a review item. When the snapshot backing a free claim goes past its refresh window the catalogue stops presenting 'verified_free' and presents 'stale' instead, and a pending review item is raised. When ingest has never published an offer in a category a provider declares 'verified_free', a pending review item is raised while the provenance-backed declaration continues to display.

f008-obsB.ruling: A stale snapshot must not sustain a published free claim (owner ruling; mechanism left to the builder).
f008-obsB.mechanism_chosen: (c) both - raise the contradiction AND downgrade the display.

measured_queue_cost.method: offline FixtureFetcher ingest + publish for all 7 provider configs against an isolated PostgreSQL, then serialize_category_matrix at now and at now+5y

f008-obsB.display_decision: 'stale', not the generic 'conflicting' collapse. Nothing is in conflict - the evidence expired. Labelling expiry as disagreement would be a guess, and 'stale' is already a first-class COVERAGE_STATE with a correct web label.

f008-obsC.ruling: The S2 deferral's stated precondition (no adapters yet) was to be re-decided once Wave 3 landed.
f008-obsC.decision: Make it material NARROWLY: only a declared 'verified_free' over a derived 'unknown'. The broad rule the deferral considered is still prohibitive.

measured_queue_cost.why_the_brief_was_wrong: Wave 3 landed adapters but the publication gate withholds every offer for 5 of the 6 merged providers (aws, azure, gcp, oracle, vercel each publish 0). 93 of 98 pairs still derive 'unknown', so the 14xN floor the deferral cited has NOT gone away.

f008-obsC.display_decision: The declaration continues to display. A 'verified_free' declaration is provenance-backed (config validation rejects an offered category with no source), and 93/98 pairs derive 'unknown' because the publication gate is conservative - not because the claim is refuted. Downgrading would suppress true free claims for an ingest-coverage reason and would move a real merged-provider verdict.

acceptance_criteria: AC1 A declared 'verified_free' whose backing snapshot is past its refresh window is a material mismatch and raises exactly one pending review item.
AC2 That pair no longer displays 'verified_free'; it displays 'stale'.
AC3 A declared 'verified_free' in a category with no published offer at all is a material mismatch and raises exactly one pending review item.
AC4 That pair still displays 'verified_free' (the declaration is provenance-backed and is not refuted by an absent publication).

AC5 Both-direction: a FRESH declared 'verified_free' over its own published Z0 offer is NOT flagged, and 'offered_no_z0'/'not_offered'/'unknown'/'incomplete'/'stale'/'conflicting' declarations over a derived 'unknown' are NOT flagged.
AC6 The derived state of every (provider, category) pair for all six merged providers is identical to main.
AC7 The DISPLAYED state of every pair for all six merged providers is identical to main at current snapshot freshness.
AC8 Every new test is proven non-vacuous by mutation, with predictions recorded before running and byte-exact restoration proven by git hash-object.
AC9 ruff check + ruff format clean; the offline pytest suite is green and no pre-existing test is weakened; the live-DB suite is green.
end_to_end_steps: Start an isolated PostgreSQL (never the shared dev stack; four builders are running).
Run the offline FixtureFetcher ingest + publish for all seven provider configs.
Serialize the category matrix at current time and at snapshot expiry; compare declared/derived/displayed for all six merged providers against the same run on main.
Run reconcile_coverage and count pending review items in each state.
migration_implications: None. Alembic head stays 0011. Nothing is persisted: the derived state is still recomputed on every read (decision Q11) and the only durable artefact remains a pending review_item.
security_privacy: No new inputs, endpoints, credentials or network access. Pure in-process rule change plus tests. No package-feed hostname or credential may reach any report, PR body, commit message or file.
portability: No new dependency, runtime or service. PostgreSQL remains the only mandatory stateful service.
z0_implications: Directly strengthens the anti-false-claim safeguard: an expired snapshot can no longer sustain a displayed free claim, and an uncorroborated free claim can no longer avoid human review. No Z0 classification rule, quota calculation or publication gate is changed.
regression_risks: MATERIAL_MISMATCHES is consumed by the public matrix, the review queue, and the reusable Wave-3 assertion helper; a broader rule would have flooded the queue with 93 items and failed several provider config suites.

The DB-free helper previously treated an unasserted category as 'nothing published'; that reading becomes a false positive once a derived 'unknown' can be material, so it now skips unasserted categories.
effective_state's generic 'conflicting' collapse would have moved two real merged-provider verdicts; the explicit display table prevents that.
negative_and_regression_tests: A fresh declared 'verified_free' over its own published Z0 offer must not be flagged (control for AC1).
A declared 'offered_no_z0' / 'not_offered' / 'unknown' over a derived 'unknown' must not be flagged (control for AC3; this is where the 91 suppressed items live).
A declared hedge ('incomplete' / 'stale' / 'conflicting') over any derivation must not be flagged.
All pre-existing MATERIAL_MISMATCHES pairs must still be material and must still display 'conflicting'.
